title: Henry Cavill’s Justice League mustache disaster is now a tongue-in-cheek Googlebook game for charity
summary: "Mustache Protocol" turns Henry Cavill's infamous CGI shave into a 16-bit Googlebook game.
body: Credit: Google TL;DR Google is launching a new series detailing what went into the creation of Henry Cavill’s Googlebook-made game. Episode one reveals that Cavill’s game is called Mustache Protocol. The game is about stopping rogue CGI artists from erasing every mustache on the planet. For every play in the month of November, Google pledges to donate $11, up to $500,000, to support and spread awareness of men’s mental health, suicide prevention, prostate cancer, and testicular cancer. Shortly after the launch of Acer’s, ASUS’, Dell’s, HP’s, and Lenovo’s Googlebooks , Google revealed it was teaming up with actor Henry Cavill to create a new game. The twist was that this game would be created directly on a Googlebook. The company is now launching a new series that details what went into the creation of this game, and the first episode has now dropped. In this episode, we learn that Cavill’s new game is titled “Mustache Protocol.” The premise is that you’re a hero who has set out to stop rogue CGI artists from erasing every mustache on the planet. This is clearly a reference to his CGI-removed mustache in the movie Justice League.
